source.title: DYNAMIX: RL-based Adaptive Batch Size Optimization in Distributed Machine Learning Systems
source.authors: Yuanjun Dai; Keqiang He; An Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of adaptive batch-size policies in distributed training, a new setting relevant to V5; reports accuracy and convergence-time comparisons against fixed-batch baselines.
record.gate_note: The study's own batch-size comparisons bear on V5. Its discussion of prior work on large-batch generalization is cited background, not an independent result. Batch-size trajectories are not separate rows because they do not report the claim's generalization outcome by batch-size condition.
record.test_reason: The study uses batch-size/generalization tradeoffs to motivate DYNAMIX and reports its performance against static baselines. Neither these comparisons nor the static batch-size sweeps hold epoch budgets fixed, so they do not establish V5's fixed-budget penalty or its removal. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: the authors report faster convergence, higher final accuracy, and reduced run-to-run variance with DYNAMIX relative to fixed-batch baselines. This does not establish V5 under fixed epoch budgets.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a PPO-based adaptive batch-size policy during distributed training; compares it with selected static batch-size baselines. The claim version's fixed-epoch comparisons and several specified recipe adaptations are not studied.
record.method_sensitivity: Results are reported across datasets, optimizers, cluster sizes, and a BytePS heterogeneous-hardware setting; static baseline batch size is selected per configuration or scale.

fits_no_version.finding: DYNAMIX achieves higher reported terminal accuracy and shorter convergence times than selected static baselines across several distributed training configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive per-worker batch scheduling can improve accuracy and time to convergence relative to selected static configurations in distributed image-classifier training.

fits_no_version.finding: Section VI-B reports ResNet34/CIFAR-100 accuracy of approximately 82% at batch size 32 versus 73% at 256, with roughly twice the convergence time for batch size 32. Epoch budgets are not matched. VGG11 baseline accuracy is ambiguously described as training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Static batch size can affect reported accuracy at convergence in distributed training; this comparison does not establish a fixed-epoch generalization penalty.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the accuracy and convergence comparisons. Fixed-batch baselines are selected as optimal configurations, and the evaluation does not hold epochs fixed; the study reports convergence-based comparisons instead.
record.rows_left_out: No further eligible batch-size versus generalization comparison results identified. Batch-size adaptation trajectories (Figure 5) do not report a separate test/generalization outcome by batch-size condition; prior-work results in the background are not this study's results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on random and natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Controlled optimizer comparisons under specified tuning regimes.

Held-out performance across batch sizes under matched epoch budgets, and whether recipe adaptations remove that penalty under comparable budgets. Convergence-based comparisons do not test these conditions.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The paper inconsistently describes accuracy as training versus validation accuracy, and supplies no numerical uncertainty estimates for the extracted comparisons. None of the method-performance improvements warrants a supports, limits_scope, or challenges verdict on V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD generalization under different tuning regimes.

Fixed epoch-budget comparisons; language models; warmup, learning-rate scaling, normalization and regularization changes; comparisons across workload-dependent batch thresholds. The study compares adaptive batch size with selected fixed-batch baselines during convergence.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.stage_stated: training from scratch; method not stated
rows.operation_detail: Fixed batch size 32 compared with DYNAMIX adaptive batch sizing; CIFAR-10, SGD.
rows.baseline: approximately 350 minutes; final accuracy approximately 0.82 across three runs
rows.note: Baseline's accuracy and time are reported for the selected trajectory; the DYNAMIX comparison says it reaches 86% in 30 minutes and outperforms both 32- and 64-batch configurations.
rows.check: Adaptive-policy performance versus a static baseline at convergence does not establish V5. Section VI-B calls the approximately 82% baseline training accuracy, despite introducing validation accuracy as the selection criterion. The later claim that static configurations reach comparable accuracy in 190 minutes is inconsistent with their reported lower terminal accuracies.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.stage_stated: training from scratch; method not stated
rows.operation_detail: Fixed batch size 64 compared with DYNAMIX adaptive batch sizing; CIFAR-10, SGD.
rows.baseline: final training accuracy ranges between 0.76 and 0.79; convergence time nearly half of batch size 32
rows.value: DYNAMIX: terminal accuracy of 86% by 30 minutes; approximately 6.3x acceleration in convergence time while maintaining equivalent or higher terminal accuracy
rows.locator: Section VI-B and VI-D; Figures 2b and 4a
rows.note: The text compares DYNAMIX to both static configurations and states the latter require approximately 190 minutes to reach comparable accuracy levels.
rows.check: No matched epoch budget; this is a DYNAMIX performance comparison. The 76–79% baseline is explicitly called training accuracy. The claimed 6.3-fold acceleration uses approximately 190/30 minutes, rather than a clearly documented time to the same accuracy.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.stage_stated: training from scratch; method not stated
rows.operation_detail: Fixed batch size 64 compared with DYNAMIX adaptive batch sizing; CIFAR-10, Adam.
rows.value: DYNAMIX: 86% accuracy within 30 minutes; 6% higher terminal accuracy
rows.note: The stated 6% higher terminal accuracy accompanies a faster convergence comparison.
rows.check: Different terminal accuracies and convergence times do not establish a large-batch penalty under fixed epochs. The improvement from 80% to 86% is six percentage points.

rows.subject: ResNet34
rows.stage_stated: training from scratch; method not stated
rows.operation_detail: Fixed batch sizes compared with DYNAMIX adaptive batch sizing; CIFAR-100, SGD.
rows.baseline: static configurations require significantly longer training periods to achieve lower terminal accuracy levels
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative baseline comparison and a DYNAMIX value.
rows.check: This compares method performance without matched epochs or a specified static batch size. The blanket assertion that static baselines have lower terminal accuracy conflicts with Section VI-B, where static batch size 32 also reaches approximately 82%.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.stage_stated: training from scratch; method not stated
rows.operation_detail: Per-cluster optimal static batch size compared with DYNAMIX; CIFAR-10, SGD.
rows.note: Comparison uses the authors' optimal static batch-size configuration for this cluster scale.
rows.check: Table I compares DYNAMIX with a selected static configuration, without matched epochs. Its times imply a 23.6% reduction, not the printed 30.1%.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.stage_stated: training from scratch; method not stated
rows.operation_detail: Per-cluster optimal static batch size compared with DYNAMIX; CIFAR-10, SGD.
rows.note: Comparison uses the authors' optimal static batch-size configuration for this cluster scale.
rows.check: Table I compares DYNAMIX with a selected static configuration, without matched epochs. Its times imply an 11.8% reduction, not the printed 13.7%.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.stage_stated: training from scratch; method not stated
rows.operation_detail: Per-cluster optimal static batch size compared with DYNAMIX; CIFAR-10, SGD.
rows.note: Comparison uses the authors' optimal static batch-size configuration for this cluster scale.
rows.check: This is adaptive-method performance against a selected static baseline, without matched epochs. Changing cluster size also changes the distributed configuration; it does not isolate V5's batch-size effect.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.stage_stated: training from scratch; method not stated
rows.operation_detail: Static batch size 64 compared with DYNAMIX adaptive batch sizing; CIFAR-10, SGD on BytePS heterogeneous hardware.
rows.value: 80%; about 16,000 seconds; 8.6% improvement on accuracy and 20% reduction in time
rows.note: Cross-platform validation using a parameter-server architecture.
rows.check: This is a cross-platform DYNAMIX performance comparison without matched epochs or a small-versus-large static batch comparison. The accuracy gain is 8.6 percentage points.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: VGG11 CIFAR-10 with SGD or ADAM, ResNet34 CIFAR-100 with SGD, VGG16 CIFAR-10 across 8, 16 and 32 nodes, and VGG11 on BytePS
